title: ShareButton
summary: The standard SwiftUI ShareLink, which opens the system share sheet. With the Monarch button style it looks like any other Monarch button. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: To send a link, text or any Transferable item to another app or person.
whenNotToUse: To put a value on the pasteboard without leaving the screen, use MonarchCopyButton.
api: ShareLink(_ title: String, item: String, subject: Text? = nil, message: Text? = nil)
static func monarch(_ variant: MonarchButtonVariant = .secondary, size: MonarchButtonSize = .md, fullWidth: Bool = false) -> MonarchButtonStyle

states.name: resting
states.description: The Monarch button in the chosen variant, with the system share symbol and the title "Share" unless a label is given.

states.name: pressed
states.description: The button's pressed colours. The share sheet opens on release.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The button's disabled colours, with disabled(_:).

appearance: The Monarch button colours in every theme. The share sheet itself is drawn by the system.
platformNotes: The web component uses the Web Share API where the browser has it and otherwise opens its own panel with the link, a Copy link button and optional targets such as email. On iOS the system share sheet is always available and already offers Copy, Mail and Messages, so the panel, the targets and the copy fallback are not needed. Android uses the system share intent in the same way.
accessibility: System behaviour: ShareLink is a button, and its default label is localised by the system.
With the Monarch button style the touch target is at least 44 by 44 points and the label scales with Dynamic Type.
An icon-only ShareLink needs a Label with a title, so VoiceOver has a name; labelStyle(.iconOnly) hides only the text.
edgeCases: The share sheet is presented by the system; an app cannot know which target was chosen.
On the Mac build host the same code shows the macOS sharing picker.
